issues.area: C2 / S3-R22 item 1 (c18 #6 not closed for the drain): one drain turn moves verdicts x followIDsPerTurn ids
issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineFollow.swift:575-580. followAfterVerdict passes a fresh `self.state.followIDsPerTurn` for every verdict. It is called at :606 (replayVerdict) and :346 (the .spaceFailure replay), inside drainEventsAfterFollow (:181-221). The batch loop breaks only when a visit leaves a rest (:200). .attemptFailed and .spaceFailure do not end a batch (:1430-1437). The drain also runs inside continueFollow's last turn (:157).
issues.problem:
Each verdict whose job's ids an apply moved since it deferred (`movesAfter`) gets a whole turn's id budget. One drain batch of up to 512 events replays every such verdict in the same actor turn, which is also the follow's last turn. A turn therefore moves up to (verdicts × 512) ids.

PROBE-C19C-DRAIN-BOUND (debug, seed 1_919_902, followIDsPerTurn = 4):
- Shape: 3 jobs, each shared by 3 prefetch members, download. v3 changes only fillers, with the follow held. Every attempt times out, so the verdicts wait. v4 gives each member its own content.
- Sweep-first: 'turns [0, 0, 9] drainTurn Optional(9)'. The drain turn moves 9 ids against a bound of 4. This holds with SyncTuning() and with (12, 4), in 2 of 2 runs.
- The answers [20 × 9] equal visit-first.

PROBE-C19C-DRAIN-C2 (release, -enable-testing):
- Shape: SyncTuning(maxConcurrentTransfers: 16, reservedInteractiveSlots: 0), which is inside concurrencyRange 1...16. 16 jobs × 500 members of one prefetch group, 8,000 ids.
- 'moved per turn [0, …, 8000]'. The drain turn held the actor [45.93, 44.23, 41.62] ms, best 41.62, at a 1-minute load of 5.61. At loads 10.57→9.88: [41.29, 41.14, 40.88]. At 8.30→8.67: [60.41, 55.73, 54.36].
- With 4 slots (2,000 ids), the best was 9.98, 9.66 and 12.46 ms in the same three runs.
issues.fix:
Bound the drain by one id budget per turn:
- Seed a FollowBudget with followIDsPerTurn. When the drain runs in continueFollow's last turn, seed it with what that turn has left.
- Pass the remaining ids into followAfterVerdict at both call sites, instead of `self.state.followIDsPerTurn`, and subtract what follow(_:ids:afterVerdict:) spent.
- When the ids are spent after an event, put the rest of the batch back at the head of eventsAfterFollow/eventStamps, exactly as the followMoving branch does. Then schedule a drain follow-up.
- A later verdict that meets a spent budget becomes a VisitRemainder through startMove(budget: 0), which already breaks the batch.

Pin it with:
- A deterministic test in both orders at followIDsPerTurn = 4, with three such verdicts (PROBE-C19C-DRAIN-BOUND's shape). Every turn moves at most 4 ids and the answers stay visit-first.
- A BenchSync release case of the 16-slot shape: best of 3 ≤ c2Budget.

issues.area: C2 / S3-R5, S3-R22 item 1: a bounded follow turn of 512 ids costs O(interests of the job) per id (10,000 user waiters sharing one content)
issues.location:
The O(interests) costs:
- Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineState.swift:711-713. Job.lane computes `interests.values.map(\.lane).max()`.
- addInterest reads it twice per join: EngineJobs.swift:133, and relane at :177 → :267.
- dropInterest (EngineJobs.swift:344-366) reads it twice. It also copies the Job (`guard var job = self.state.jobs[transfer]`), so `job.interests[token] = nil` copies the whole interests dictionary.

Each id reaches them from continueMove: EngineMoves.swift:208 (reroute → addInterest) and :214 (removeInterest).

Both costs are pre-existing at s3-base (EngineState.swift:502 and EngineJobs.swift:239 there). Cycle 19's id bound does not cover them.
issues.problem:
Shape (PROBE-C19C-USER-SHARED-C2 and -TURNS, release, -enable-testing): BenchSync.sharedApplyTurns' convergence shape with one user-initiated waiter per id instead of a prefetch group. 10,000 ids share H's content, one interest token each. O, a user job, downloads (held). v3 maps every id to O.

Every follow turn moves exactly 512 ids, yet at a 1-minute load of 7.21→8.00:
- Superseding shape: per turn [6.6, 8.32, 9.71, 11.25, … 31.73, 33.69, 19.0] ms. The cost grows with O's interests. Heartbeat best of 3: 33.31 ms ([33.78, 33.54, 33.31]).
- `keep` shape: one more id of H's content stays, so H is not superseded and each emptied interest goes through removeInterest. Per turn [66.4, 64.41, 63.0, … 38.33, 19.52] ms. The apply's window took 70.87 ms. Heartbeat best of 3: 103.11 ms ([103.11, 177.20, 182.00]).

The id bound assumes about 5 µs per id (EngineMoves.swift:121-126). Here each id costs O(n) lane scans and, in `keep`, a dictionary copy.

By reading (not probed), a drain batch of 512 deferred joins onto one job with many interests costs the same.
issues.fix:
Make a job's lane O(1):
- Keep per-lane interest counts on Job, updated on every interest insert, removal and lane change. heldLane is unchanged.
- Make dropInterest remove the interest in place (`self.state.jobs[transfer]?.interests[token] = nil` and so on), with no live copy of the Job.

Then re-measure, and pin with a BenchSync release case of both shapes (10,000 user waiters sharing one content; superseding, and one id kept): best of 3 ≤ c2Budget.

issues.area: Flakiness (close-out bar 1(d)): barrierReadmitsBehindTheOwedVisitsPlaces failed in the coverage run
issues.location: Tests/ZTronAssetSyncTests/Engine/EngineFollowBarrierReplayTests.swift:92, the followVisitedFirst case. FollowBarrier.apply's visit-first branch (Tests/ZTronAssetSyncTests/Engine/EngineFollowBarrierTests.swift:97-109) returns at `!followOwed`.
issues.problem:
The coverage run (`swift test --enable-code-coverage --skip Benchmarks`, the instrumented debug build) recorded: 'recorded an issue with 1 argument visit → .followVisitedFirst at EngineFollowBarrierReplayTests.swift:92:9: Expectation failed: started.first == n.transferID'. A member (c-cd9e41e8…) started before N. The bundle ended with '✘ Test run with 552 tests in 53 suites failed after 336.355 seconds with 1 issue.' The 1-minute load over that bundle averaged about 31 (13 to 68).

The same commit passed this test in verify --quick, Sync ×3, TSan and the iOS Simulator run, and in 20 of 20 isolated debug repeats at loads 47 to 70. The test is old (40d9711) and unchanged in cycle 19.

The mechanism is not confirmed. By reading: the visit-first branch returns once no follow is owed, while the barrier can still be up for a drain turn. If any event waited for v3's follow, `releaseReadmissionFollowUps()` runs before the drain's pump. The re-admission is then replayed in the drain, and the 7 members' older queue places come ahead of N.
issues.fix:
Record `eventsAfterFollow.count`, `drainFollowUpScheduled` and `followBarrier` when FollowBarrier.apply's visit-first branch returns. Then repeat the Sync bundle under --enable-code-coverage until it fails, or until 5 runs pass.

- If a drain turn is pending there, make the branch wait for `!followBarrier && !drainFollowUpScheduled`, which is what visit-first means.
- Otherwise make this test wait for N's start before releasing the re-admission follow-up.

Keep both assertions (G3), and re-run the coverage bundle 3 times.

issues.area: Hardening (unproven): continueMove re-checks a holder by TransferID only
issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineMoves.swift:179-183 (`guard self.state.jobs[holder] != nil`). MoveProgress, VisitRemainder and InboundMove.progress carry no holder epoch.
issues.problem:
TransferIDs are derived from content. Suppose a holder is removed between two turns, for example when an owed move in continueInbound, which runs first, takes its last ids. If a re-route of an id mapped back to that content then re-creates it, the next turn continues the old holder's moves on the new job.

By reading, the per-interest guards (EngineMoves.swift:202-206) make the stale items no-ops on the new job, and I found no answer difference. This is not probed.
issues.fix: Record the holder's epoch in MoveProgress, and end the moves when `jobs[holder]?.epoch` differs. Epochs do not change behind the barrier, since no attempt starts there. Alternatively, record in the draft why the guards make it safe.

issues.problem:
findInbound's lookups for content without a checksum can be reached through the pass path that S3-R24 names. The draft's reason ('no path we found leaves the id on another job while the target runs') is refuted. PROBE-C19R-LEGACY-TARGET (seed 1_919_902, tuning 5/2) builds the path:
1. T is zz-x's entry without a checksum (16 B), with user waiter A. T publishes, held at its first unit.
2. v3 maps zz-x to C and is visited in full. T's visit passes T and A stays on T.
3. B's request joins H, C's job, which is downloading and held.
4. v3b changes only fillers; v4 maps zz-x back to T; v5 changes only the later fillers.
5. Sweep-first, v5's walk records 'c-7dba52ac... -> l-73839f2e...: [zz-x]' (H -> T) through byIdentifier.
At HEAD it passes 4/4: A and B are both served T's 16 B, and T's content starts once. byIdentifierTargetDrop and byIdentifierLookupDrop each fail 2/2, in both followUpsFirst cases, at the walk's expectation ('Expectation failed: atWalk', VerifyC19ReqsLegacyProbes.swift:94 in the mutant logs, :99 in the saved copy). The sweep-first case asserts the walk's move H -> T [zz-x]; both cases assert the answers (A and B served T's bytes, one start of T). Kill both drop-mutants 2/2, and replace the draft's 'Not reached' entry with the test and its mutant rows.

issues.location: Sources/ZTronAssetSync/Engine/EngineFollow.swift:1248-1249 (waitingTarget: case .queued, .blocked, .downloading: return nil; line 1249 has 0 hits); docs/adr-drafts/s3f.md:4395-4397
issues.problem: No test reaches the branch, and the fix neither removed it nor argued it equivalent. The draft's own reason concedes a window: a failed publication that is re-queued keeps its epoch until its next start, 'which the barrier holds back'. enqueue's doc (EngineJobs.swift:470-473) lists a publication's ENOENT re-queue as a path that queues at once behind the barrier. So an owed move's target can sit queued at the move's epoch while followedLane's carried() reads it.
issues.fix:
Choose one and record it in the draft:
- Reach it in both orders: the target publication is re-queued while an owed move onto it is pending, and a lane decision, such as a 429 on the carried id's lane, reads carried(). Kill the drop-mutant 2/2.
- Remove it, turning the assumption into a followBarrierViolations clause that a test exercises.
- Argue it equivalent per S3-R19 item 2.

The test fails on the iOS Simulator in both orders.
Failures:

Cause, by reading the code:
- The test reads the fake transport's '.started' record order (RecordingFakes.swift:545, via starts at :466).
- Each attempt task writes that record in drive at remote.transfer (EngineDispatch.swift:807), and only after awaiting answeredFromStore (:781).
- With SyncTuning()'s 4 slots and 1 reserved, three prefetch attempts are in flight together. Sweep-first, one barrier-end pump admits N and two members, because pump() admits nothing behind the barrier or during the drain (EngineDispatch.swift:95-104). Visit-first, N's attempt is still in its store read when the follow-up's pump admits two members.
- So the three records race. The same three ids head both failures, in different orders.
No difference in the engine's own dispatch order is shown, and an order-only difference would be non-blocking under S3-R16 item 2. But a test that fails in a run is blocking.
issues.fix:
Make the observation deterministic without losing the assertion (G3), and record the change in the draft. Either:
- give the test one slot, SyncTuning(maxConcurrentTransfers: 1, reservedInteractiveSlots: 0), as its neighbouring order tests (:107, :198) already do; or
- assert the engine's order instead of the transport's records, i.e. N's queue ticket below each re-queued member's.
